candidates.snippet: paper_id=arxiv-2609.31992 | paper_version=arXiv:2609.31992v1 [cs.LG], 25 Sep 2026 (PDF, 5 pages) | title=Mechanistic Interpretability Reveals Shared Causal Subspaces in Brain-to-Speech Decoders | authors=Maryam Maghsoudi, Ayushi Mishra, Sanghamitra Dutta | venue=arXiv preprint, arXiv:2609.31992v1 [cs.LG] | source_url=https://arxiv.org/pdf/2609.31992v1 | abstract=Decoding covert speech, such as mimed or imagined, from brain activity is harder than decoding vocalized speech. Cross-modal transfer, where information from one speech form helps decode another, is a promising remedy; yet how a decoder internally represents and processes brain activity from different speech forms remains unclear. In this work, we ask: which internal neurons of a decoder carry cross-modal information, and are these neurons shared across different speech forms? To answer these questions, we leverage mechanistic interpretability, using recordings of the same sentences in vocalized, mimed, and imagined input pairs for activation patching. We insert the decoder’s internal activity for a sentence in one condition into its processing of the same sentence in another and measure the change in decoding accuracy. We find that no single neuron drives this benefit; instead, it arises from small groups of neurons, with vocalized speech as the most useful source. These groups are largely condition-specific in the early stage of the decoder but overlap in the later stage. These findings point toward more data-efficient covert speech decoders through training objectives that encourage shared later-stage representations learned mainly from vocalized data. | tags=mechanistic interpretability, activation patching, brain-to-speech decoding, covert speech, sEEG | evidence_family=primary_source (arXiv preprint PDF) | review_state=source_checked | review_basis=arXiv 2609.31992v1 PDF, 5 pages, pypdf text extraction with page delimiters, arXiv abstract page metadata (title/authors/date) | source_coverage={'confirmed': ['title/authors/abstract (p.1)', '§1 Introduction (pp.1–2)', 'Fig.1 decoder and patching schematic (p.2)', 'Fig.2 single-neuron ΔPCC distribution (p.2)', '§2 Preliminaries and Approach (pp.2–3)', 'Fig.3 top-k saturation curves (p.3)', '§3 Results (pp.3–4)', 'Fig.4 cross-source Jaccard overlap (p.4)', '§4 Discussion and Limitations incl. footnote 2 (p.4)', '§5 References (p.5)'], 'unconfirmed_or_approximate': ['exact per-k curve values in Fig.3/Fig.4 (axis-level reading only)', 'small print inside Fig.2 axis labels'], 'not_present': ['supplementary material, code, or data links — none present in the PDF']} | needs_manual_check=Ground-truth mel-spectrogram y provenance for mimed/imagined targets (no overt audio)., sEEG acquisition parameters, participant details, and decoder training hyperparameters live in VocalMind [15], not restated here., Figure-read numbers (∼0.8, 0.3–0.4, 0.4–0.6, 5–8×) are approximate. | Study.study_design=controlled_experiment | Study.research_objective=Identify which internal neurons of a brain-to-speech decoder carry cross-modal information (vocalized/mimed/imagined) and whether those neurons are shared across conditions;
